record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Geometric realization of the reduction system
record.original_question: For the finite-dimensional integrable system generated by the commuting integrals in equation (9), find a geometric realization by passing to flat coordinates, or generalized flat coordinates in the constant-curvature case, and then express both the potential and the associated Nijenhuis operator M from Remark 2.3 in those coordinates.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Find a geometric realization of the integrable system generated by (9).

Take a flat coordinate system, or a generalised flat coordinate system if the metric has constant nonzero curvature, and find the potential and the corresponding Nijenhuis operator M discussed in Remark 2.3 in these coordinates.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with a (1,1)-tensor field $L\colon TM\to TM$ whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y)=L^2[X,Y]-L[LX,Y]-L[X,LY]+[LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically, and assume $L$ is gl-regular (its minimal and characteristic polynomials coincide pointwise). Let $g$ be a pseudo-Riemannian metric on $M$ that is geodesically compatible with $L$, meaning that $g$ and the metric $g\circ L^{-1}$ have proportional unparametrised geodesics (equivalently, the Sinjukov / Benenti-type compatibility equations hold). Assume that $g$ has either zero curvature or constant nonzero sectional curvature.

In a neighbourhood of a gl-regular point one obtains a family of $n=\dim M$ functionally independent functions $F_1,\dots,F_n$ in involution with respect to the canonical Poisson structure on $T^*M$, of the form
$$F_k(x,p)=\tfrac{1}{2}\,g^{ij}_{(k)}(x)\,p_ip_j+U_k(x),\qquad k=1,\dots,n, \tag{9}$$
where the leading symbols $g^{ij}_{(k)}$ are built from $g$ and the powers of $L$ in the standard way, and $\{U_k\}$ are scalar potentials determined (up to constants) by the compatibility equations. Let $M$ denote the Nijenhuis (1,1)-tensor naturally associated to this finite-dimensional integrable system (the "secondary" Nijenhuis operator obtained from $L$ and $g$ via the geodesic-compatibility construction).

Problem. Provide an explicit geometric realisation of the finite-dimensional integrable system $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ defined by (9). More precisely:

(a) Choose a flat coordinate system $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ for $g$ when $g$ is flat, or a generalised flat coordinate system when $g$ has constant nonzero curvature.

(b) In these coordinates, write down explicit formulas for the potentials $U_k(x)$ appearing in (9).

(c) In the same coordinates, write down an explicit formula for the components of the associated Nijenhuis operator $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research problem in the 2024 problem list on Nijenhuis geometry and integrable systems. No subsequent work giving an explicit geometric realisation with potentials and the associated Nijenhuis operator in (generalised) flat coordinates was found.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V: Geodesic Equivalence and Finite-Dimensional Reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Every metric g geodesically compatible with L gives a finite-dimensional reduction of this PDE system.
status_evidence.claim: Background construction underlying the problem; no explicit flat-coordinate realisation of the full reduction is provided.
